_comment: Tokyo Night (night) for glow's markdown rendering, with Visual Studio
Dark+ inside fenced code blocks. Palette reference: docs/tokyonight.md.
The split is the repo's usual one -- chrome is Tokyo Night, code is Dark+
-- and here the two meet inside one document. Headings, links, rules and
quotes are chrome. A fenced block is code, and `bat README.md` highlights
that same fence, so the chroma table below is bat's Visual Studio Dark+
rather than VS Code's published Dark+: reading a file through glow and
through bat should not recolour it.
glamour parses this with encoding/json, which drops keys it does not know
without a word -- the same trap as yazi's theme. The key names here are
the json tags in charmbracelet/glamour ansi/style.go, all of them; check
against that file if a setting ever seems to stop applying. (This
_comment key is itself dropped, which is how it can be here at all.)
This is a whole style, not an overlay. WithStylePath unmarshals the file
into an empty StyleConfig -- nothing is merged in from glamour's own dark
style -- so every prefix, indent and format below has to be carried even
though none of them is a colour. Drop `item.block_prefix` and the bullets
stop appearing.
Code blocks are approximate and cannot be otherwise: glamour hardcodes
chromaFormatter = "terminal256" and glow never calls WithChromaFormatter,
so the chroma table below is rounded to the 256-colour cube on the way out
(#569cd6 lands on #5fafd7). The markdown chrome above it is true 24-bit.
If glamour ever takes the colour profile into account there, these values
become exact with no change here.
